question.text: Capital gains on equity MF (holding > 12 months) post Jul 2024:

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the income-tax framework applicable from 23 July 2024, long-term capital gains on equity-oriented mutual fund units (held more than 12 months) are taxed at 12.5%, with an annual exemption threshold of Rs. 1.25 lakh aggregated across listed equity shares and equity-oriented MF units. The Trap: The earlier regime taxed equity LTCG at 10% above a Rs. 1 lakh threshold under Section 112A; that combination has been superseded. A blanket 15% rate applies to short-term equity capital gains, not long-term. "No tax" ignores the LTCG levy altogether. Note: The Portfolio Managers (NISM-Series-XXI-B) workbook supports the classification of equity-oriented MF units held more than 12 months as long-term capital assets but does not state the current 12.5% rate or the Rs. 1.25 lakh threshold introduced from July 2024. Those values reflect current Indian tax law (Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024) used here as general regulatory framing.
